simple: a storage device that you read and write in fixed-size pieces, each with a number.
analogy: the warehouse, where every box space has a number in the ledger.
precise: a device presenting storage as an array of equal-sized logical blocks addressed by number; reads and writes transfer whole blocks.
source: D3 of F1-49 (Randal Bryant, David O'Hallaron, "Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective" (tier 3; curriculum reading-list item 1): the storage technologies section (disk geometry, disk operation and access time, logical disk blocks, solid-state disks)); D4 of F1-49 (Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces" (OSTEP; tier 3; curriculum reading-list item 2): the chapters on hard disk drives and on flash-based SSDs (pages and blocks, FTL, garbage collection, write amplification, wear levelling, trim)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a sector is one numbered piece of a disk; the LBA is its number.
analogy: the number of a box space in the ledger.
precise: the host addresses a drive by LBA, a block number starting at 0; byte offset = LBA × logical block size. The drive maps LBAs to physical locations itself.
source: D4 of F1-49 (Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces" (OSTEP; tier 3; curriculum reading-list item 2): the chapters on hard disk drives and on flash-based SSDs (pages and blocks, FTL, garbage collection, write amplification, wear levelling, trim)); D5 of F1-49 (INCITS T13, "ATA/ATAPI Command Set" (ACS) (tier 1; curriculum item 41): logical and physical sector sizes in IDENTIFY DEVICE data; data set management); R2 of F1-49 (R2 — lab run of Listing 2 (lba.log), same toolchain, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a disk that stores data magnetically on spinning plates.
analogy: the old hall with the turntable and the ladder.
precise: a drive with one or more rotating platters, read/write heads on an actuator arm, data in concentric tracks divided into sectors.
source: D3 of F1-49 (Randal Bryant, David O'Hallaron, "Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective" (tier 3; curriculum reading-list item 1): the storage technologies section (disk geometry, disk operation and access time, logical disk blocks, solid-state disks)); D4 of F1-49 (Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces" (OSTEP; tier 3; curriculum reading-list item 2): the chapters on hard disk drives and on flash-based SSDs (pages and blocks, FTL, garbage collection, write amplification, wear levelling, trim)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the time to move the head to the right ring, then the time to wait for the data to spin under it.
analogy: sliding the ladder, then waiting for the turntable.
precise: HDD access time = seek time + rotational latency + transfer time; average rotational latency is half a revolution.
source: D3 of F1-49 (Randal Bryant, David O'Hallaron, "Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective" (tier 3; curriculum reading-list item 1): the storage technologies section (disk geometry, disk operation and access time, logical disk blocks, solid-state disks)); D4 of F1-49 (Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces" (OSTEP; tier 3; curriculum reading-list item 2): the chapters on hard disk drives and on flash-based SSDs (pages and blocks, FTL, garbage collection, write amplification, wear levelling, trim)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: chips that keep data without power and without moving parts.
analogy: the drawers of lockers in the new hall.
precise: non-volatile memory built from floating-gate or charge-trap transistor cells, organised into pages (the unit of read and program) grouped into blocks (the unit of erase).
source: D4 of F1-49 (Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces" (OSTEP; tier 3; curriculum reading-list item 2): the chapters on hard disk drives and on flash-based SSDs (pages and blocks, FTL, garbage collection, write amplification, wear levelling, trim)); D3 of F1-49 (Randal Bryant, David O'Hallaron, "Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective" (tier 3; curriculum reading-list item 1): the storage technologies section (disk geometry, disk operation and access time, logical disk blocks, solid-state disks)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: flash cannot be overwritten; it must be erased first, and only whole blocks can be erased.
analogy: a full locker cannot be refilled; you empty whole drawers.
precise: programming can only move cells from the erased state toward the programmed state; returning them requires a block erase.
source: D4 of F1-49 (Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces" (OSTEP; tier 3; curriculum reading-list item 2): the chapters on hard disk drives and on flash-based SSDs (pages and blocks, FTL, garbage collection, write amplification, wear levelling, trim)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a drive made of flash chips plus a small computer that manages them.
analogy: the new hall and Amira with her ledger.
precise: a drive whose controller runs firmware that maps logical blocks to flash pages, cleans blocks, spreads wear, corrects bit errors and talks to the host over an interface such as SATA or NVMe.
source: D4 of F1-49 (Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces" (OSTEP; tier 3; curriculum reading-list item 2): the chapters on hard disk drives and on flash-based SSDs (pages and blocks, FTL, garbage collection, write amplification, wear levelling, trim)); D6 of F1-49 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 6 hardware catalog, storage rows (ATA/ATAPI, AHCI, NVMe, SCSI and SAS, UFS, eMMC and SD, virtio storage)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the part of the SSD's firmware that hides the erase rules from the computer.
analogy: Amira's ledger and her nightly tidying.
precise: the mapping from logical pages to physical flash pages with out-of-place updates, garbage collection and wear levelling.
source: D4 of F1-49 (Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces" (OSTEP; tier 3; curriculum reading-list item 2): the chapters on hard disk drives and on flash-based SSDs (pages and blocks, FTL, garbage collection, write amplification, wear levelling, trim)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: cleaning: copy the still-useful pages out of a block, then erase the block.
analogy: the nightly tidy-up of a drawer.
precise: FTL process that selects a victim block, relocates its valid pages and erases it to create free pages. Not the same as garbage collection of memory in programming languages.
source: D4 of F1-49 (Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces" (OSTEP; tier 3; curriculum reading-list item 2): the chapters on hard disk drives and on flash-based SSDs (pages and blocks, FTL, garbage collection, write amplification, wear levelling, trim)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: how many pages the flash really wrote for each page you asked to write.
analogy: boxes moved by the warehouse divided by boxes the restaurant delivered.
precise: WA = flash page writes ÷ host page writes; extra writes come from garbage-collection copies.
source: D4 of F1-49 (Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces" (OSTEP; tier 3; curriculum reading-list item 2): the chapters on hard disk drives and on flash-based SSDs (pages and blocks, FTL, garbage collection, write amplification, wear levelling, trim)); R1 of F1-49 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F1-49/ftl.log), toolchain g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, exit code 0. A simulator: its numbers describe the toy model only) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: spreading erases evenly so no block wears out early.
analogy: using every drawer in turn instead of always the one by the door.
precise: FTL policy that balances program/erase cycles across blocks, because each block survives a limited number of erase cycles.
source: D4 of F1-49 (Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces" (OSTEP; tier 3; curriculum reading-list item 2): the chapters on hard disk drives and on flash-based SSDs (pages and blocks, FTL, garbage collection, write amplification, wear levelling, trim)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a message from the computer: "these blocks no longer hold anything I need".
analogy: the restaurant phoning to say "throw away the boxes on these shelves".
precise: a host command (named differently per interface) that tells the drive which logical blocks are unused, so the FTL can treat their pages as invalid.
source: D4 of F1-49 (Remzi Arpaci-Dusseau, Andrea Arpaci-Dusseau, "Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces" (OSTEP; tier 3; curriculum reading-list item 2): the chapters on hard disk drives and on flash-based SSDs (pages and blocks, FTL, garbage collection, write amplification, wear levelling, trim)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the language a computer uses to talk to fast SSDs over PCI Express.
analogy: the restaurant's order board and done board system with the warehouse.
precise: a family of specifications by NVM Express, Inc. defining a register interface, queue-based command submission and completion, an admin command set and I/O command sets for non-volatile memory controllers.
source: D1 of F1-50 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 42; version to be recorded): controller registers; queue mechanics (submission and completion queues, head and tail, full and empty, phase tag); admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue); D3 of F1-50 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Command Set Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 42): Read, Write, Flush; namespaces) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a ring of command slots in the computer's memory, filled by the driver.
analogy: the circular order board.
precise: a circular buffer of fixed-size command entries in host memory; the host writes entries at the tail, the controller fetches them from the head.
source: D1 of F1-50 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 42; version to be recorded): controller registers; queue mechanics (submission and completion queues, head and tail, full and empty, phase tag); admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a ring of "done" slots in the computer's memory, filled by the device.
analogy: the circular done board.
precise: a circular buffer in host memory into which the controller posts completion entries (command identifier, status, SQ head pointer, phase tag); one CQ may serve several SQs.
source: D1 of F1-50 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 42; version to be recorded): controller registers; queue mechanics (submission and completion queues, head and tail, full and empty, phase tag); admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a device register the driver writes to say "there is new work" or "I have read up to here".
analogy: the bell wired to the warehouse counter, with a number display. Not the same as the faculty's "doorbell" analogy for interrupts, which ring the other way (device to CPU, F1-42).
precise: a memory-mapped controller register holding a queue's new SQ tail or CQ head index.
source: D1 of F1-50 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 42; version to be recorded): controller registers; queue mechanics (submission and completion queues, head and tail, full and empty, phase tag); admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue); D2 of F1-50 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVMe PCIe Transport Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 42): doorbell registers and PCI Express specifics); R3 of F1-50 (R3 — QEMU pci_nvme_* trace of SeaBIOS (version 1.16.3-debian-1.16.3-2, as it printed itself) reading LBA 0, plus the boot sector's debug-console line (nvme_trace.log), exit code 33 as designed. Emulated controller only: untested on a physical SSD) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one bit in each completion that flips every time the device goes round the ring.
analogy: the clerk's ink colour, changed each lap of the board.
precise: a bit the controller writes in each completion entry, inverted on each pass through the CQ, so the host can tell new entries from stale ones without clearing memory.
source: D1 of F1-50 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 42; version to be recorded): controller registers; queue mechanics (submission and completion queues, head and tail, full and empty, phase tag); admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue); R1 of F1-50 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F1-50/nvme_ring.log), toolchain g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, exit code 0. A model, not a driver) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one special queue pair for managing the drive, and other queue pairs for reading and writing data.
analogy: the manager's board and the cooks' boards.
precise: queue pair 0 carries admin commands (Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue…); I/O queue pairs, created through the admin queue, carry I/O commands such as Read and Write.
source: D1 of F1-50 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 42; version to be recorded): controller registers; queue mechanics (submission and completion queues, head and tail, full and empty, phase tag); admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue); R3 of F1-50 (R3 — QEMU pci_nvme_* trace of SeaBIOS (version 1.16.3-debian-1.16.3-2, as it printed itself) reading LBA 0, plus the boot sector's debug-console line (nvme_trace.log), exit code 33 as designed. Emulated controller only: untested on a physical SSD) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one numbered "disk" inside the NVMe drive.
analogy: one named storage area of the warehouse.
precise: a quantity of non-volatile memory addressed by logical blocks, identified by a namespace ID (nsid); I/O commands name the nsid they act on.
source: D1 of F1-50 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 42; version to be recorded): controller registers; queue mechanics (submission and completion queues, head and tail, full and empty, phase tag); admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue); D3 of F1-50 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Command Set Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 42): Read, Write, Flush; namespaces) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the memory address inside a command that tells the drive where to put or take the data.
analogy: the shelf number written on the order.
precise: a pointer to a host physical memory page used to describe a command's data buffer; QEMU's trace prints it as prp1 and prp2.
source: D1 of F1-50 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 42; version to be recorded): controller registers; queue mechanics (submission and completion queues, head and tail, full and empty, phase tag); admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue); R3 of F1-50 (R3 — QEMU pci_nvme_* trace of SeaBIOS (version 1.16.3-debian-1.16.3-2, as it printed itself) reading LBA 0, plus the boot sector's debug-console line (nvme_trace.log), exit code 33 as designed. Emulated controller only: untested on a physical SSD) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the number the driver gives each command so it can match the answer.
analogy: the request number on the order.
precise: a value chosen by the host in each submission entry and returned in the matching completion entry.
source: D1 of F1-50 (NVM Express, Inc., "NVM Express Base Specification" (tier 1; curriculum item 42; version to be recorded): controller registers; queue mechanics (submission and completion queues, head and tail, full and empty, phase tag); admin commands Identify, Create I/O Completion Queue, Create I/O Submission Queue); R3 of F1-50 (R3 — QEMU pci_nvme_* trace of SeaBIOS (version 1.16.3-debian-1.16.3-2, as it printed itself) reading LBA 0, plus the boot sector's debug-console line (nvme_trace.log), exit code 33 as designed. Emulated controller only: untested on a physical SSD) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one packet as it travels on an Ethernet link: addresses, type, data and a check value.
analogy: the sealed box with destination, sender, meal and tamper sticker.
precise: the IEEE 802.3 unit of transmission: destination address, source address, a type/length field, the payload (padded to a minimum size), and a 32-bit frame check sequence; preceded on the wire by a preamble and a start delimiter.
source: D1 of F1-51 (IEEE, "IEEE 802.3" (Ethernet; tier 1; curriculum item 106, free through the IEEE GET Program): frame format and FCS clause; MAC and PHY layering; auto-negotiation; MDIO management registers (clause 22 and clause 45)); D3 of F1-51 (W. Richard Stevens (with Kevin Fall), "TCP/IP Illustrated, Volume 1" (tier 3; curriculum item 49): the link-layer and ARP chapters; network byte order) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the 6-byte name of a network interface.
analogy: the address label on the box.
precise: a 48-bit address; one bit marks group (multicast/broadcast) versus individual addresses, another marks locally administered versus globally unique ones; all-ones is the broadcast address.
source: D1 of F1-51 (IEEE, "IEEE 802.3" (Ethernet; tier 1; curriculum item 106, free through the IEEE GET Program): frame format and FCS clause; MAC and PHY layering; auto-negotiation; MDIO management registers (clause 22 and clause 45)); R2 of F1-51 (R2 — tshark decode of Listing 1's pcap (frame_decode.log), TShark (Wireshark) 4.2.2, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a number in the frame that says what kind of data is inside.
analogy: "meal" or "cutlery" written on the box.
precise: the 2-byte type field after the addresses; tshark decoded 0x0806 as ARP and 0x0800 as IPv4 in this build's captures.
source: D1 of F1-51 (IEEE, "IEEE 802.3" (Ethernet; tier 1; curriculum item 106, free through the IEEE GET Program): frame format and FCS clause; MAC and PHY layering; auto-negotiation; MDIO management registers (clause 22 and clause 45)); R2 of F1-51 (R2 — tshark decode of Listing 1's pcap (frame_decode.log), TShark (Wireshark) 4.2.2, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a 4-byte number computed from the whole frame, used to detect damage.
analogy: the tamper sticker whose pattern depends on the contents.
precise: a CRC-32 over the frame from the destination address to the end of the padding, appended by the transmitting MAC and checked by the receiving MAC, which drops frames whose FCS does not match.
source: D1 of F1-51 (IEEE, "IEEE 802.3" (Ethernet; tier 1; curriculum item 106, free through the IEEE GET Program): frame format and FCS clause; MAC and PHY layering; auto-negotiation; MDIO management registers (clause 22 and clause 45)); R2 of F1-51 (R2 — tshark decode of Listing 1's pcap (frame_decode.log), TShark (Wireshark) 4.2.2, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the part of the network hardware that builds and checks frames.
analogy: Rosa in the dispatch office.
precise: the data-link-layer block that frames data, generates and checks the FCS, filters by destination address and moves frames to and from memory (with the DMA engine of the NIC, F1-52).
source: D1 of F1-51 (IEEE, "IEEE 802.3" (Ethernet; tier 1; curriculum item 106, free through the IEEE GET Program): frame format and FCS clause; MAC and PHY layering; auto-negotiation; MDIO management registers (clause 22 and clause 45)); D5 of F1-51 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 6 catalog row "Ethernet MAC and PHY" and the C9/C12 milestones) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the chip that turns bits into signals on the cable and back.
analogy: Kwame at the loading dock.
precise: the physical-layer chip or block that encodes and decodes the line signal, negotiates speed and duplex with the link partner (auto-negotiation) and reports link state in management registers.
source: D1 of F1-51 (IEEE, "IEEE 802.3" (Ethernet; tier 1; curriculum item 106, free through the IEEE GET Program): frame format and FCS clause; MAC and PHY layering; auto-negotiation; MDIO management registers (clause 22 and clause 45)); D5 of F1-51 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 6 catalog row "Ethernet MAC and PHY" and the C9/C12 milestones) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the sets of wires that carry frame data between a MAC and a PHY.
analogy: the handover hatch between office and dock.
precise: media-independent interfaces between MAC and PHY; RGMII forwards a clock with the data and uses both clock edges; SGMII is a serial variant (curriculum catalog).
source: D1 of F1-51 (IEEE, "IEEE 802.3" (Ethernet; tier 1; curriculum item 106, free through the IEEE GET Program): frame format and FCS clause; MAC and PHY layering; auto-negotiation; MDIO management registers (clause 22 and clause 45)); D2 of F1-51 (The RGMII interface specification (an industry document originating at HP, as named by the curriculum catalog; tier 1): clock-forwarded double-data-rate interface and the required clock-to-data delay); D5 of F1-51 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 6 catalog row "Ethernet MAC and PHY" and the C9/C12 milestones) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a slow two-wire bus the MAC's driver uses to read and set the PHY's registers.
analogy: the office's telephone to the dock.
precise: the management interface of IEEE 802.3 (register sets of clause 22 and clause 45) used to read link status and configure the PHY.
source: D1 of F1-51 (IEEE, "IEEE 802.3" (Ethernet; tier 1; curriculum item 106, free through the IEEE GET Program): frame format and FCS clause; MAC and PHY layering; auto-negotiation; MDIO management registers (clause 22 and clause 45)); D5 of F1-51 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 6 catalog row "Ethernet MAC and PHY" and the C9/C12 milestones) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the PHYs at both ends agree they are connected.
analogy: both dock lights green.
precise: the PHY's link-status indication, reached after auto-negotiation; it says nothing about whether the MAC–PHY data path delivers good frames.
source: D1 of F1-51 (IEEE, "IEEE 802.3" (Ethernet; tier 1; curriculum item 106, free through the IEEE GET Program): frame format and FCS clause; MAC and PHY layering; auto-negotiation; MDIO management registers (clause 22 and clause 45)); D5 of F1-51 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 6 catalog row "Ethernet MAC and PHY" and the C9/C12 milestones) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the network card or chip of a computer.
analogy: the back door with its courier and parcel rack.
precise: a device, on PCs attached over PCIe, containing at least a MAC (often also a PHY), packet buffers, DMA engines, descriptor rings and interrupt logic; the driver controls it through registers in a BAR.
source: D1 of F1-52 (Intel, "PCI/PCI-X Family of Gigabit Ethernet Controllers Software Developer's Manual" (8254x family, the e1000; tier 1; named in the curriculum's C9 milestone): receive and transmit descriptor rings, head and tail registers, interrupt causes, missed-packet counting); R2 of F1-52 (R2 — QEMU 8.2.2 monitor info pci for e1000, e1000e and virtio-net, with pci.ids lookups (qemu_nics.log), exit code 0. Emulated devices; untested on a physical NIC) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a small record in memory that tells the NIC where a packet buffer is and, after use, what happened to it.
analogy: one shelf with its crate and flag.
precise: a fixed-size structure (16 bytes for the e1000e descriptors in this chapter's trace) holding a buffer's physical address, a length and command/status bits; the NIC reads it by DMA and writes status back.
source: D1 of F1-52 (Intel, "PCI/PCI-X Family of Gigabit Ethernet Controllers Software Developer's Manual" (8254x family, the e1000; tier 1; named in the curriculum's C9 milestone): receive and transmit descriptor rings, head and tail registers, interrupt causes, missed-packet counting); R3 of F1-52 (R3 — QEMU 8.2.2 e1000e trace events while the iPXE boot ROM did DHCP, with tshark 4.2.2's list of the same run's frames (ring_trace.log), exit code 124 (time limit, as designed). Emulated device; untested on a physical NIC) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a circular list of descriptors shared by the driver and the NIC.
analogy: the round rack of shelves.
precise: a contiguous array of descriptors in host memory whose base address and length are written to NIC registers; the NIC and driver advance around it, wrapping at the end; separate rings exist for transmit and receive.
source: D1 of F1-52 (Intel, "PCI/PCI-X Family of Gigabit Ethernet Controllers Software Developer's Manual" (8254x family, the e1000; tier 1; named in the curriculum's C9 milestone): receive and transmit descriptor rings, head and tail registers, interrupt causes, missed-packet counting); D4 of F1-52 (Jonathan Corbet, Alessandro Rubini, Greg Kroah-Hartman, "Linux Device Drivers", 3rd edition (tier 3): the chapters on DMA and on network drivers) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
related: Head and tail (of a NIC ring)

term: Head and tail (of a NIC ring)
simple: two slot numbers that split the ring into "NIC's part" and "driver's part".
analogy: the courier's position and the red marker.
precise: the head is advanced by the NIC as it consumes descriptors; the tail is written by the driver to hand descriptors to the NIC; the NIC uses the slots from head up to, not including, tail.
source: D1 of F1-52 (Intel, "PCI/PCI-X Family of Gigabit Ethernet Controllers Software Developer's Manual" (8254x family, the e1000; tier 1; named in the curriculum's C9 milestone): receive and transmit descriptor rings, head and tail registers, interrupt causes, missed-packet counting); R1 of F1-52 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F1-52/ring.log), g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a device reading or writing the computer's memory by itself, without the CPU copying each byte.
analogy: the courier walking to the shelf himself.
precise: bus-master transactions (on PCIe: memory read and write requests from the device) addressed with physical or I/O-virtual addresses that the driver provided.
source: D4 of F1-52 (Jonathan Corbet, Alessandro Rubini, Greg Kroah-Hartman, "Linux Device Drivers", 3rd edition (tier 3): the chapters on DMA and on network drivers); D6 of F1-52 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 6 catalog rows "PCIe" and "Ethernet MAC and PHY", and milestone C9 (e1000 driver)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
related: Head and tail (of a NIC ring)

simple: the NIC's signal to the CPU that something happened, for example a packet arrived.
analogy: the kitchen bell.
precise: a legacy pin interrupt, MSI or MSI-X message raised when an enabled cause bit is set in the NIC's interrupt cause register; the driver reads the causes and handles the rings.
source: D1 of F1-52 (Intel, "PCI/PCI-X Family of Gigabit Ethernet Controllers Software Developer's Manual" (8254x family, the e1000; tier 1; named in the curriculum's C9 milestone): receive and transmit descriptor rings, head and tail registers, interrupt causes, missed-packet counting); D4 of F1-52 (Jonathan Corbet, Alessandro Rubini, Greg Kroah-Hartman, "Linux Device Drivers", 3rd edition (tier 3): the chapters on DMA and on network drivers); R3 of F1-52 (R3 — QEMU 8.2.2 e1000e trace events while the iPXE boot ROM did DHCP, with tshark 4.2.2's list of the same run's frames (ring_trace.log), exit code 124 (time limit, as designed). Emulated device; untested on a physical NIC) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a packet the NIC had to throw away because the driver had given it no free buffer.
analogy: a parcel sent back at the red marker.
precise: a receive drop counted by the NIC when head reaches tail; the frame never reaches memory or the operating system.
source: D1 of F1-52 (Intel, "PCI/PCI-X Family of Gigabit Ethernet Controllers Software Developer's Manual" (8254x family, the e1000; tier 1; named in the curriculum's C9 milestone): receive and transmit descriptor rings, head and tail registers, interrupt causes, missed-packet counting); R1 of F1-52 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F1-52/ring.log), g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the queue format of virtio devices, the "paravirtual" devices made for virtual machines.
analogy: a rack designed for couriers who are part of the same company.
precise: a ring structure defined by the VIRTIO specification, shared between a guest driver and a host device, with buffers described in a descriptor table and an "available" and a "used" ring; QEMU's virtio-net NIC uses it.
source: D3 of F1-52 (OASIS, "Virtual I/O Device (VIRTIO)" specification (tier 1): virtqueues and the network device); R2 of F1-52 (R2 — QEMU 8.2.2 monitor info pci for e1000, e1000e and virtio-net, with pci.ids lookups (qemu_nics.log), exit code 0. Emulated devices; untested on a physical NIC) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one computer's network card reading or writing another computer's memory directly.
analogy: the partner's driver using the service door and the sealed shelf.
precise: network transfers executed by the NICs between registered memory regions of two hosts, with the data placed by DMA directly in application buffers, without copies through the operating system and, for one-sided operations, without target-CPU involvement per transfer.
source: D1 of F1-53 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification", Volume 1, with the RoCE v2 annex (tier 1; curriculum item 81): transport, queue pairs, memory regions and keys, one-sided and two-sided operations); D3 of F1-53 (NVIDIA (formerly Mellanox), "RDMA Aware Networks Programming User Manual" (tier 2): concepts and programming examples); D5 of F1-53 (W. Richard Stevens (with Kevin Fall), "TCP/IP Illustrated, Volume 1" (tier 3), and "Linux Device Drivers", 3rd edition (tier 3), network-driver chapter: the ordinary receive path through the kernel) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a piece of a program's memory that the program has announced to its NIC, with rules about who may use it.
analogy: the sealed shelf with its rules.
precise: an address range pinned in physical memory and entered in the NIC's translation and protection tables, with access flags (for example local write, remote write, remote read); registration returns a local key and a remote key.
source: D1 of F1-53 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification", Volume 1, with the RoCE v2 annex (tier 1; curriculum item 81): transport, queue pairs, memory regions and keys, one-sided and two-sided operations); D2 of F1-53 (rdma-core project documentation and manual pages (libibverbs, librdmacm; tier 2): the verbs API, registration, the Linux device directory) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the number another computer must quote to use a registered region.
analogy: the card number 1100.
precise: a key the target's NIC checks on each incoming one-sided request, together with the requested address range and operation; a request that fails a check completes with a remote access error.
source: D1 of F1-53 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification", Volume 1, with the RoCE v2 annex (tier 1; curriculum item 81): transport, queue pairs, memory regions and keys, one-sided and two-sided operations); R1 of F1-53 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F1-53/rdma.log), g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a send queue and a receive queue that a program uses to give the NIC work for one connection.
analogy: the driver's order book and the restaurant's list of free crates.
precise: a send queue and a receive queue of work requests in memory shared with the NIC, connected to a queue pair on the remote host (for the reliable connected transport); the program posts work requests and rings a doorbell, as with the rings of F1-50 and F1-52.
source: D1 of F1-53 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification", Volume 1, with the RoCE v2 annex (tier 1; curriculum item 81): transport, queue pairs, memory regions and keys, one-sided and two-sided operations); D3 of F1-53 (NVIDIA (formerly Mellanox), "RDMA Aware Networks Programming User Manual" (tier 2): concepts and programming examples) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: where the NIC reports finished work.
analogy: the driver's receipt book.
precise: a queue of completion entries that the NIC writes when work requests finish, polled by the program; one-sided operations produce completions only on the requesting side.
source: D1 of F1-53 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification", Volume 1, with the RoCE v2 annex (tier 1; curriculum item 81): transport, queue pairs, memory regions and keys, one-sided and two-sided operations); R1 of F1-53 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F1-53/rdma.log), g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: one-sided: only the requester takes part; two-sided: both sides take part.
analogy: the driver putting a crate on the sealed shelf versus a cook signing for a delivery.
precise: RDMA WRITE and RDMA READ name a remote address and key and complete without action by the target program; SEND consumes a receive buffer the target program posted in advance and produces a completion at both ends.
source: D1 of F1-53 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification", Volume 1, with the RoCE v2 annex (tier 1; curriculum item 81): transport, queue pairs, memory regions and keys, one-sided and two-sided operations); R1 of F1-53 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F1-53/rdma.log), g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: two kinds of networks that carry RDMA.
analogy: a private road built for the service vans, and the same vans on the public road.
precise: InfiniBand is a network architecture with its own links, switches and transport defined by the InfiniBand Trade Association; RoCE v2 (RDMA over Converged Ethernet) carries the InfiniBand transport inside UDP/IP over Ethernet.
source: D1 of F1-53 (InfiniBand Trade Association, "InfiniBand Architecture Specification", Volume 1, with the RoCE v2 annex (tier 1; curriculum item 81): transport, queue pairs, memory regions and keys, one-sided and two-sided operations); D6 of F1-53 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 14 (Track F) rows "Inter-node networks" and "GPUDirect" and the Track F hardware note, and the university guide's DS401 course description) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an RDMA NIC reading or writing a GPU's memory directly.
analogy: the service door opening straight into the pastry room instead of the cold room.
precise: a mechanism with which a PCIe NIC performs DMA to and from GPU device memory, avoiding a copy through host memory; named in curriculum Track F.
source: D4 of F1-53 (NVIDIA, "GPUDirect RDMA" documentation (tier 2), and the ROCm documentation on GPU-aware networking for the AMD side); D6 of F1-53 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 14 (Track F) rows "Inter-node networks" and "GPUDirect" and the Track F hardware note, and the university guide's DS401 course description) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: dynamic power is used each time transistors switch; static power leaks away even when nothing switches.
analogy: gas burned while cooking, and the pilot flames that burn all night.
precise: dynamic power of CMOS logic is about α·C·V²·f (activity factor, switched capacitance, supply voltage, clock frequency); static power comes from leakage currents and grows with temperature.
source: D1 of F1-54 (David A. Patterson, John L. Hennessy, "Computer Organization and Design" (tier 3): the sections on dependability and Hamming codes, and on the power wall); D2 of F1-54 (David Money Harris, Sarah L. Harris, "Digital Design and Computer Architecture" (tier 3): power consumption (dynamic and static power)) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: running a chip slower and at lower voltage when full speed is not needed or is too hot.
analogy: turning burners down to a simmer.
precise: changing a chip's clock frequency together with the lowest supply voltage that is safe at that frequency; on PCs exposed as performance states (P-states) controlled by the OS or the hardware.
source: D2 of F1-54 (David Money Harris, Sarah L. Harris, "Digital Design and Computer Architecture" (tier 3): power consumption (dynamic and static power)); D7 of F1-54 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 6 catalog rows "Thermal management and hardware monitoring", "Processor power management (P-, C-, S-states)", "Platform power on Arm: PSCI and SCMI" and "Memory controllers and DRAM", milestones B2 and C15) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: slowing a chip down automatically when it gets too hot.
analogy: Ana slowing the line on a hot evening.
precise: reduction of frequency, voltage or duty cycle triggered when a temperature sensor passes a limit, by hardware, firmware or the OS, to keep the chip below its maximum junction temperature.
source: D2 of F1-54 (David Money Harris, Sarah L. Harris, "Digital Design and Computer Architecture" (tier 3): power consumption (dynamic and static power)); D7 of F1-54 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 6 catalog rows "Thermal management and hardware monitoring", "Processor power management (P-, C-, S-states)", "Platform power on Arm: PSCI and SCMI" and "Memory controllers and DRAM", milestones B2 and C15) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: an area with a temperature sensor, and temperatures at which something must happen.
analogy: the kitchen's thermometer and the numbers on Ana's rule.
precise: ACPI describes thermal zones with methods for the current temperature (_TMP) and trip points for passive cooling (_PSV), critical shutdown (_CRT) and hibernate (_HOT), as listed in the curriculum's catalog.
source: D4 of F1-54 (UEFI Forum, "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) Specification" (tier 1): thermal zones and processor and system power states); D7 of F1-54 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 6 catalog rows "Thermal management and hardware monitoring", "Processor power management (P-, C-, S-states)", "Platform power on Arm: PSCI and SCMI" and "Memory controllers and DRAM", milestones B2 and C15) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: memory that stores extra check bits so that it can fix small errors.
analogy: Tomás's check digits.
precise: a memory system in which the memory controller stores check bits computed from each data word and, on every read, uses them to correct some errors and detect others; reported to software as corrected or uncorrected errors.
source: D1 of F1-54 (David A. Patterson, John L. Hennessy, "Computer Organization and Design" (tier 3): the sections on dependability and Hamming codes, and on the power wall); D3 of F1-54 (John L. Hennessy, David A. Patterson, "Computer Architecture: A Quantitative Approach" (tier 3): power and energy, dependability, DRAM organisation and ECC) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: a code that fixes any one wrong bit in a word and notices any two.
analogy: check digits that fix one faded digit and flag two.
precise: a Hamming code extended by one overall parity bit; for 64 data bits it needs 8 check bits, a (72,64) code, as Listing 1 builds and tests.
source: D1 of F1-54 (David A. Patterson, John L. Hennessy, "Computer Organization and Design" (tier 3): the sections on dependability and Hamming codes, and on the power wall); R1 of F1-54 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F1-54/secded.log), g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the number the decoder computes that says where the error is.
analogy: the line-and-column pointer Tomás gets from the check digits.
precise: for a Hamming code, the XOR of the positions of all 1 bits in the received word (equivalently, the recomputed check bits XOR the stored ones); zero means no detected error, otherwise it names the flipped position if there was exactly one flip.
source: D1 of F1-54 (David A. Patterson, John L. Hennessy, "Computer Organization and Design" (tier 3): the sections on dependability and Hamming codes, and on the power wall); R1 of F1-54 (R1 — lab run of Listing 1 (university/labs/F1-54/secded.log), g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0, exit code 0) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
related: CE and UE (corrected and uncorrected errors)

term: CE and UE (corrected and uncorrected errors)
simple: errors the memory fixed by itself, and errors it could only report.
analogy: a fixed faded digit, and a line that cannot be trusted.
precise: error classes reported by memory controllers through the machine-check architecture and operating-system drivers (Linux EDAC); a CE is logged and counted, a UE in data being used is fatal to that data and commonly to the process or the system.
source: D5 of F1-54 (Intel, "Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual", Volume 3, machine-check architecture and power and thermal management chapters; AMD, "AMD64 Architecture Programmer's Manual" (tier 1)); D6 of F1-54 (The Linux kernel documentation and source (tier 4): the EDAC subsystem and drivers, RAS, and the thermal and hwmon frameworks); D7 of F1-54 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 6 catalog rows "Thermal management and hardware monitoring", "Processor power management (P-, C-, S-states)", "Platform power on Arm: PSCI and SCMI" and "Memory controllers and DRAM", milestones B2 and C15) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)

simple: the processor's alarm for a hardware error it cannot hide.
analogy: closing the restaurant for the night.
precise: an exception (#MC on x86, prepared for in Track B's IDT set-up) raised by the machine-check architecture when hardware detects an error, with details in machine-check bank registers.
source: D5 of F1-54 (Intel, "Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual", Volume 3, machine-check architecture and power and thermal management chapters; AMD, "AMD64 Architecture Programmer's Manual" (tier 1)); D7 of F1-54 (Systems Curriculum (this project), section 6 catalog rows "Thermal management and hardware monitoring", "Processor power management (P-, C-, S-states)", "Platform power on Arm: PSCI and SCMI" and "Memory controllers and DRAM", milestones B2 and C15) — pending verification (dossier gate G1 open)
related: CE and UE (corrected and uncorrected errors)
